items.summary: Singaporean Loh Woei Min argues that the push for Healthier Choice symbols and dietary certifications is pushing stalls to swap traditional fats, meats and broths for standardised substitutes. As Singapore nominates local heroes for the Singapore Hawkers' Awards 2026, he warns against superficial fusion and premiumisation—over-engineered mooncakes or truffle-stuffed bak chang—that mask lost craftsmanship while inflating prices.
items.title: Don't Let Compliance Dilute Authentic Hawker Flavours

items.summary: After a North Korea–linked breach stole US$6.3 billion in October, Binance aims to reopen withdrawals for all networks by next week and has covered 95% of losses. The FBI attributes the hack to Pyongyang's TraderTraitor group, though it is denied. Bitcoin fell to a four-month low near US$62,112 amid ETF outflows, liquidations totaling about US$2 billion in one day, and speculation that Anthropic's IPO may be diverting capital from crypto.
items.title: Binance Aims to Reopen Withdrawals After North Korea–Linked $6.3 Billion Hack; Crypto Slumps Continue

items.summary: On Nov 15, Megaspeed said Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang had officially left the company on Aug 30, 2025. The Singapore-based Nvidia Asia-Pacific cloud partner faces scrutiny after reports that Jensen Huang had an affair with her and US suspicions she was a spy. In Oct 2025, the New York Times reported Megaspeed under investigation over helping Chinese customers obtain export-controlled chips; China denied it, and no violations were found.
items.title: Megaspeed Says Alice Huang Left Company in August 2025

items.summary: Economist John Quiggin argues that despite recent announcements of large-scale job losses at NAB, Qantas, Canva and Atlassian attributed to AI, an economic 'job apocalypse' is unlikely. He contends these moves reflect routine business practices—such as banks hiring and dismissing staff opportunistically—and offshoring rather than automation. While software firms like Canva face genuine disruption from accessible design tools, others remain resilient.
items.title: Is the AI job apocalypse finally here? The evidence suggests otherwise | John Quiggin

items.summary: Han Won-seok, a 34-year-old who scored 397. 5 out of 400 in the first round of South Korea's certified tax accountancy exam with only one of 160 questions wrong, admitted cheating using a microcamera to photograph test questions, an AI tool and his smartphone. Confessing via video on lawyer Lee Don-Ho's YouTube channel after reconsidering how his conduct harmed other candidates, Han apologized to fairly passing entrants. The Ministry of Employment and Labour and the Human Resources Development Service held an emergency meeting; new measures will revoke qualifications and ban offenders from retaking the exam for five years if AI is used to cheat.
items.title: South Korea's Top Tax Accountancy Exam Candidate Admits Cheating With Camera, Phone and AI

items.summary: A software reporter rejects AI DJ commentary from both YouTube Music's "Beyond the Beat" and Spotify, finding it interrupts rather than enhances listening. She disliked YouTube's 30-second expository interjections—such as its mispronunciation of Charli XCX—and Spotify's filler-word-laden voices that triggered an uncanny-valley reaction. Though she found Spotify's commentary tighter, neither experience was enjoyable enough to return.
items.title: AI DJs Completely Kill My Groove

items.summary: Daehwa Kim, a fifth-year PhD student in Carnegie Mellon's Future Interfaces Group, created Object Agent Twins (OATs), micro-agent AI avatars displayed on tiny E Ink screens that pair with household objects. Presenting the project at the ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology in Detroit in early November—where she earned two Honorable Mention awards—Kim aimed to bring the care-driven joy of 1990s Tamagotchi pets into physical life, countering constant smartphone screen dependence. The hardware costs around $20 for its main module and uses sensors tracking moisture, temperature, humidity, light, occupancy, motion, and sound; sprites are generated via Google Gemini's Nano Banana service. Users can name their OAT and customize behaviors through a web portal. Kim reports three common use patterns: sensing exploitation (e. g. , a coffee machine), warning of hazards like 3D-printer fumes, and self-tracking such as weightlifting on a dumbbell.
items.title: AI Tamagotchi Turns Everyday Objects Into Needy Virtual Pets

items.summary: AI tools now let developers generate code and ship features far faster than before, yet running that software remains labor-intensive: teams must still monitor, maintain, and fix it. Google's 2025 DORA report surveyed nearly 5,000 technology professionals and found greater AI adoption correlated with quicker delivery but lower stability; the researchers did not prove AI code directly caused more outages. Ishay Yaari of DataAgent notes that more code, frequent deployments, and infrastructure changes create more failure points, forcing SRE teams to investigate logs and recent changes before deciding what to fix.
items.title: AI speeds software delivery but strains its stability and upkeep

items.summary: San Francisco voice-AI company Bland released Tofu-1, its first full-duplex speech-to-speech model in research preview. Unlike cascade agents that convert speech to text and back, Tofu-1 listens while speaking, reasoning during calls with no transcript intermediary—targeting noisy environments like cars, hospitals, and weak signals. It offers audio skills including speaker tracking, noise separation, and paralinguistics detection.
items.title: Bland Launches Tofu-1 Full-Duplex Speech-to-Speech Model for Calls

items.summary: A Texas energy giant is preparing to pump carbon dioxide underground near the rural, predominantly Black community of Cheek outside Beaumont. The project could be the first operating one in the state and a milestone for an industry that promotes carbon capture and storage as a climate tool; regulators won federal permitting authority late last year and approved Exxon Mobil's project in September. Nearby residents distrust assurances about groundwater safety, fearing contamination or suffocation from leaks, while some experts call the technology more of a distraction than effective. Companies have canceled nearly a third of 19 proposed Texas projects so far. Supporters argue storage fits an all-of-the-above approach and cite federal tax credits plus East Texas' pipeline network and geology; Exxon has seven agreements covering emissions equal to those from 2 million cars.
items.title: Texas Approves First Carbon Storage Project Near Black Community as Residents Question Safety

items.summary: Wildfire litigation has become a multibillion-dollar enterprise, with more than $18 billion awarded or agreed to in civil settlements for victims across California, Hawaiʻi, Colorado and Oregon since 2017. Utilities such as PG&E, PacifiCorp, Xcel Energy and Southern California Edison have borne the brunt of these claims. The Camp Fire near Paradise, sparked by a faulty Pacific Gas and Electric transmission tower in November 2018, led to an $13.5 billion settlement that drove the company into bankruptcy. Lawsuits increasingly target utilities nationwide; some Colorado residents sued San Isabel Electric Association over the Aspen Acres Fire, which destroyed more than 320 homes. California’s strict-liability inverse condemnation standard has fueled soaring claims, prompting firms like Singleton Schreiber to specialize in wildfire cases—recovering $3 billion for over 30,000 victims and employing around 200 staff. Mass torts are handled via contingency fees of roughly 30–40 percent, though Hawaiʻi caps reasonable fees at 25 percent; the Maui settlement reached $4 billion with attorneys capped at $222 million. Wall Street funders offering loans above 20 percent annualized interest have drawn criticism, as states and utilities weigh intervention to curb payouts.
items.title: How Wildfire Litigation Became Big Business in America

items.summary: Noel Tata, chairman of the Tata Trusts and a key figure in the Tata Group, questioned whether the conglomerate has enough discipline to execute its ambitious investment projects. Speaking at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi on Saturday, he said the group's strategic direction remains sound but stressed the need for discipline in executing large projects and allocating capital. He clarified that he had not questioned their strategy or direction, only sometimes questioning delivery.
items.title: Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata Questions Execution Discipline of Group's Mega Projects

items.summary: Alan Milburn's final report on young people and work warns that almost a million youth are not in education, employment or training. Austerity, the pandemic, AI disruption and soaring living costs compound the crisis, with unemployment among under-25s rising fastest since 2008 to reach its highest level relative to all ages since the early 1990s; young people now account for about 40% of unemployment. Milburn proposes benefit cuts for under-25s in exchange for a legal guarantee of work or training, noting that £25 goes on benefits for every £1 spent on job support. However, caveats remain: half of Neets are not on benefits, and poor-quality jobs plus automation pose bigger threats than generous benefits.
items.title: Milburn Report and Britain's Youth Jobs Crisis

items.summary: Discount retailer Poundland, owned by US investors Gordon Brothers, launched 'Operation Gloria' to restock 600 shops with 16m grocery items after filing for administration. With a high-court deadline of 26 November looming, £21m was released from an accused £50m hoard while talks continue. Gordon Brothers faces accusations of predatory conduct despite claims it saved the business bought for £1; preferred bidder Martin Property Group's progress stalled over loan terms.
items.title: Poundland's Emergency Restock and Rescue Talks Amid Owner Disputes

items.summary: Hong Kong property developer New World Development proposed a rights issue on Sunday, Nov. 15, raising about HK$24. 9 billion ($3. 17 billion) amid tight credit conditions and a weak market. Controlling shareholder Chow Tai Fook Enterprises (CTFE), which owns roughly 45. 3% of the company, committed to take up its full entitlement and underwrite remaining shares for up to HK$18. 7 billion. Proceeds will prepay about 10% (~HK$82 billion) of bank loans while extending the rest by two years, repay debt including senior notes and perpetual securities, and fund resumed dividends when permitted.
items.title: New World Development Proposes HK$24.9 Billion Rights Issue to Cut Debt and Bolster Liquidity

items.summary: Anand Mahindra described Bihar as a potential 'tourism gold mine,' urging greater traveller attention to its historical and cultural heritage. A video of Rajgir prompted him to explore the state's ancient history, Buddhist legacy and modern attractions.
items.title: Mahindra Calls Bihar a Tourism Gold Mine

items.summary: Chinese Premier Li Qiang called on Chinese and Thai enterprises to elevate bilateral cooperation from "dining tables and taste buds" to digital intelligence and green development, urging both sides to strengthen industrial synergy and supply chain integration while moving up the global value chain. Speaking at a Bangkok symposium with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, Li cited high-level mutual trust, growing connectivity through infrastructure like the China-Thailand railway and Pinglu Canal, and expanding innovation cooperation as opportunities for deeper economic ties. He emphasized traditional agricultural trade alongside emerging fields such as artificial intelligence, clean energy, and biomedicine. Anutin described China as Thailand's most important trading partner and called for expanded collaboration in electric vehicles, agriculture, investment, and connectivity.
items.title: China and Thailand Pursue Higher-Level Cooperation in Digital and Green Sectors

items.summary: Italy's data protection agency fined Meta Platforms about €805 million (roughly $887 million) after finding that a Facebook app feature accessed Android users' photos and videos without consent, affecting around 20 million Italian users. Meta has 60 days to disable the feature by default and obtain separate consent. The fine equals roughly 0.47% of global revenue. Meta plans to appeal, calling it disproportionate.
items.title: Italy Fines Meta $887 Million Over Android Users' Data Access

items.summary: SpaceX's Starship Ship 42, nicknamed "Don't Panic," completed its 15th flight test and longest mission to date on November 13-14, 2026. After more than 22 hours in space, it returned Saturday and was caught for the first time by the launch tower's mechanical arms at Starbase, Texas. The spacecraft deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites before reentry. CEO Elon Musk praised the recovery as "looks great," while NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman called it "almost magic."
items.title: Starship Achieves First Mechanical-Arm Catch in Flight Test

items.summary: The article opens with a cookie and privacy notice, then shifts to how fishermen adapt as nearshore catches dwindle. A larger boat ferries smaller boats farther offshore; once there, they fish independently. For Feng Ping of Jinqing Dao—first met 12 years ago—fishing is no longer his only livelihood.
items.title: Farming the Sea — Feng Ping's Changing Livelihood on Jinqing Dao

items.summary: The article describes a new offshore fishing method in which large vessels transport fishermen, supplies and smaller fishing boats farther from shore. Once the fleet reaches distant fishing grounds, the smaller boats operate independently—some diving into the water while others fish with rods. This arrangement lets crews reach more remote areas and adapt to changing sea conditions.
items.title: Big Boats, Small Boats, Farther Seas

items.summary: Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan and Egypt condemned a fresh Iranian drone attack on the US radar system at Al-Riffa air base in Bahrain. The IRGC claimed responsibility for six drones targeting the facility hosting the US Navy's Fifth Fleet. Negotiations to end the war remain stalled as Iran maintains its naval blockade of Hormuz while the US enforces economic pressure.
items.title: Iranian Drone Strikes on Bahrain Air Base Spark Regional Condemnation Amid Stalled Iran-US War

items.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo's son, Cristianinho, made his Portugal Under-17 debut on Thursday, playing the final 20 minutes of a 4-0 European Championship qualifying win over Andorra. The 16-year-old Al Nassr forward had progressed through the Under-15 and Under-16 ranks with 13 appearances before this step up at a moment of generational change in Portuguese football.
items.title: Ronaldo Jr Makes Portugal Under-17 Debut as His Father Retires Internationally

items.summary: FRANCE 24 reviews striking images from the week, including angry Spanish protests over a housing crisis dominating its election campaign, Pope Leo XIV's visit to his adopted homeland Peru, and Rocky fans marking 50 years since the boxing classic was released.
items.title: The week in pictures: Spain protests, Pope Leo's Peru 'homecoming' and Rocky fans in Philly

items.summary: Russian officials confirmed Sunday that Nizhnekamsk, a city of about 240,000 people dubbed the 'petrochemical capital' of Tatarstan, endured prolonged Ukrainian airstrikes overnight. The attack damaged industrial facilities and a residential building, sparking a fire at the Sibur-owned Nizhnekamskneftekhim complex and wounding three people. Separate strikes killed an engineer at a Taganrog substation.
items.title: Ukrainian Drones Strike Russia's Petrochemical Capital in Overnight Assault

items.summary: Romanian authorities confirmed that three commercial vessels were struck Saturday evening by drones off the country's Black Sea coast near the Sulina canal, a key shipping route used by Ukraine to export goods. No injuries were reported as crews extinguished onboard fires. Romanian Prime Minister Luca Niculescu condemned the attacks as unacceptable and a violation of international law, attributing them to Russia's war against Ukraine.
items.title: Romania Reports Drone Attacks on Three Commercial Vessels Near Black Sea Coast

items.summary: A Jordanian court sentenced three men—two brothers and their brother-in-law—to death by hanging for a fatal mass shooting on 23 October at St George's church in Hmoud, Karak governorate. The attack killed nine people during a Christian funeral and injured 34 others. Convicted of terrorist acts, the attackers fled before being located three days later.
items.title: Three Men Sentenced to Death in Jordan Over Church Mass Shooting

items.summary: Singapore data center firm Megaspeed International says suspected spy Alice Huang left in August 2025. It faces allegations of routing Nvidia chips to China and denies the claims, saying reports lack verifiable evidence. Jensen Huang acknowledged an undisclosed affair before resigning as CEO; his board will investigate. Singapore police say chip-laden servers were exported to Malaysia amid ongoing probes.
items.title: Megaspeed Denies China Chip-Smuggling Allegations as Alice Huang Exits Firm

items.summary: The Canary Islands recorded a record daily arrival of 1,488 migrants on Saturday (14 November), exceeding the previous high of 1,461 people set on 7 November 2020. Over two days, 2,331 people arrived across 22 boats, overwhelming island resources per President Fernando Clavijo.
items.title: Record Immigration Day in El Hierro as 1,488 Arrive in Canary Islands

items.summary: Tomoya Masaki and Rui Muneyama could not split the MVP award at the Asia Professional Baseball Championship, but shared the title with their Samurai Japan teammates. In Sunday's final at Tokyo Dome before 36,022 fans, Masaki hit a three-run homer as Hiroto Takahashi threw seven frames of one-run ball to lead Japan past South Korea 5-1.
items.title: Samurai Japan Wins Asia Professional Baseball Championship Over South Korea

items.summary: Southeast Asian leaders opened their annual summit in Manila on Sunday, with world leaders expected to focus over three days on trade, energy and conflict—including the war in Iran. Donald Trump is anticipated to arrive in Manila on Tuesday. Details are reported by FRANCE 24 correspondent Tommy Walker from Bangkok.
items.title: Philippines and Australia Strengthen Joint Military Deterrence at ASEAN Summit

items.summary: Flavio Bolsonaro fled Brazil after losing the presidential election to Lula da Silva, despite a travel ban and surrender deadline tied to corruption and money-laundering investigations. He told The Epoch Times he plans permanent US residency through legal means, saying he can defend Brazil from abroad while maintaining contact with supporters. Trump welcomed him; Brazilian media report court probes over film financing and links to lawyer Willer Tomaz.
items.title: Brazil's Bolsonaro Seeks Permanent US Residency After Election Defeat

items.summary: At the Rugby League World Cup final on 11 September, Australia's Kangaroos defeated New Zealand 32-10 at Lang Park. Jamayne Isaako kicked off into touch and Liam Martin scored the fastest try in World Cup final history after just 88 seconds, setting an aggressive tone. Despite a steady opening spell where both teams matched each other, New Zealand collapsed from the 15th to the 35th minute, completing only one set amid numerous errors. Australia's speed, led by Munster and Grant, overwhelmed the Kiwis in Brisbane's humid conditions.
items.title: Australia Crush New Zealand in World Cup Final at Lang Park

items.summary: The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) Center reported on Sunday, 15 November 2026, that a tanker was attacked while transiting the Arabian Gulf eastbound toward the Strait of Hormuz. UKMTO cited an Indian Shipping Authorities report and stated via X that the crew are accounted for and safe. The extent of damage and any environmental impact remain unknown, with vessels urged to exercise caution.
items.title: Tanker Under Attack in Gulf Waters

items.summary: A study by researchers with Kristian Skrede Gleditsch and Gudmund Hermansen examines how mass mobilisation—defined as sustained, organised protests involving more than 1,000 people aimed at regime change—influenced democratic transitions between 1900 and 2019. Using time-varying statistical models focused on autocracies, they find that protest effectiveness peaked in a golden age from the early 1980s to roughly 2011, when mobilisation strongly correlated with both regime collapse and democratisation. Before 1980 it toppled regimes without reliably producing democracy; after 2011 authoritarian leaders increasingly survived large-scale protests. The authors reject several single-factor explanations—campaign size, participant diversity, leadership, repression, geography—and note their measures are crude. They suggest social-media dependence, smarter repression via new technologies, and a post–Arab Spring shift toward stability over reform may contribute, but cannot decisively test these or explain the rise and fall of effectiveness.
items.title: The Golden Age of Mass Mobilisation and Democratic Change (1980s–2011)

items.summary: South Africa faces a potentially difficult summer as an established El Niño is expected to strengthen into a super event by late 2026, with effects continuing into early 2027. This raises risks of drought, heatwaves, water stress and loss of grazing for livestock. Agricultural researchers at Cedara in the KwaZulu-Natal Midlands tested when to plant fodder radish under rainfed conditions without fertiliser, reflecting smallholder constraints. They found earlier planting—December versus January—yielded more tubers or leafy feed with higher protein and mineral content including phosphorus, potassium and zinc. The findings suggest farmers should treat planting as a window rather than a fixed date to maximise nutritious feed from rainfall alone amid declining pastures.
items.title: Super El Niño could leave South Africa short of grazing. Timing of livestock fodder crops is crucial

items.summary: Jordan's State Security Court sentenced three men to death for a deadly shooting at a Greek Orthodox Church in Karak last month, per state-run Al Mamlaka TV. The October 23 attack was one of the deadliest on Jordan's Christian minority in decades, killing nine people and wounding dozens more. Attackers targeted mourners attending a funeral; authorities identified the three defendants as two brothers and their brother-in-law, followers of an extremist ideology but not affiliated with an organized group. Arrested three days after the attack following a shootout with security forces, no group claimed responsibility for the assault.
items.title: Jordan Sentences Three Men to Death Over Deadly Church Attack

items.summary: Haitians have welcomed the deployment of around 2,000 Salvadoran troops to help combat gang violence. President Nayib Bukele said his soldiers will launch an offensive from a stadium in Port-au-Prince that gangs had controlled for two years following the 2021 assassination of President Jovenel Moïse. Experts say many Haitians support this hardline approach as conditions remain desperate, though the troops operate outside the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force.
items.title: Haitians Welcome Salvadoran Troops Amid Gang Violence

items.summary: During his visit to the Afro-Peruvian city of Zaña, Pope Leo XIV denounced the suffering and humiliation endured by enslaved Africans whose descendants continue facing discrimination. The city preserves memory of generations torn from their homes into slavery, an estimated 100,000 brought to Peru over more than 170 years since emancipation. With African ancestry himself, Leo modelled his ministry on St Turibius of Mogrovejo's example.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Denounces Suffering of African Enslaved People in Peru

items.summary: A drone attack on a military base in Santa Rosa del Sur killed at least three soldiers and wounded dozens, marking one of the deadliest incidents of 2026. Since President Abelardo de la Espriella took office in August, drone-related deaths among security forces have more than tripled, from eight to over twelve. The Ideas for Peace Foundation records 351 attacks this year alone—roughly one every 21 hours—with guerrilla groups like the ELN and Mordisco advancing their technology faster than state defenses can respond. Colombia lacks a system capable of stopping these drones, with purchased equipment detecting threats only at dangerously short range.
items.title: How Colombia is losing the war on drones

items.summary: In Quito on October 14, Natalia Peñaherrera’s home lost power for over two hours during an electricity crisis the government had denied. For her grandmother with pulmonary fibrosis, whose oxygen battery barely held out until lights returned, such blackouts are a matter of life and death. Ecuadorians face layered hardship: bureaucratic obstacles, corruption scandals like Progen’s $104 million in repainted generators, and pervasive fear of extortion. Latinobarómetro data reveals deep disillusionment—only 16% (vs. 28% regional) trust hospitals; just 11% (vs. 22%) the justice system; only 31% see anti-corruption progress. State efficiency scores 4.4 out of 10, below Latin America’s 4.7 average.
items.title: Life in Ecuador Under Crisis and Distrust

items.summary: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, once a dishwasher at a San Jose Denny's where the company idea was conceived in 2015, had a plaque removed before being reinstated on Sept. 26, 2023 by CEO Kelli Valade. The removal came amid allegations forcing his resignation over affairs with Alice Huang and Kimberly Powell.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Denny's Plaque Removed and Reinstalled Amid Nvidia Resignation Scandal

items.summary: Singapore-based cloud firm Megaspeed rejected media reports about its business, supply chain and global operations, calling them unsupported by evidence while launching an internal investigation. The controversy centers on allegations that it routed restricted Nvidia chips to China via Southeast Asia in violation of US export controls. It also emerged amid claims linking Alice Huang to Chinese intelligence and Jensen Huang's extramarital ties; Trump was reportedly briefed before Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on November 12, calling his departure sad.
items.title: Megaspeed Denies Nvidia Export Allegations as Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Spy Claims

items.summary: Hindustan Times' evening brief recaps five top stories. Megaspeed says Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang left on August 30, 2025 amid the Jensen-Huang affair controversy. US prosecutors seek 293 months (about 24 years) for Nikhil Gupta over an alleged plot to kill Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York. A Bengaluru cab driver killed seven family members, with motives including a ₹3 crore property dispute and gold sale. Air India restored non-stop Delhi-Mumbai-to-New York flights after airspace reopened. India beat New Zealand by 22 runs in the fifth ODI at Mount Maunganui, ending NZ's seven-year home streak.
items.title: HT Evening News Brief Nov 15: Megaspeed breaks silence on Alice Huang amid Nvidia row; India clinch ODI series vs New Zealand

items.summary: Natalia Rachelson, Senior Vice President of Applications Development at Oracle, told PTI that businesses should measure AI success by the improvement it delivers rather than the number of agents deployed. She urged leaders to set measurable goals—such as reducing accounting errors or transport costs—and establish a baseline first. The biggest gains come from redefining processes where work is delayed; for example, cutting 10,000 steps down to five when AI handles middle stages. Rachelson cautioned against the misconception that AI merely does existing tasks faster, cheaper and better. She noted people remain in charge throughout, with agents operating within defined boundaries.
items.title: Oracle's Natalia Rachelson on Measuring AI by Results

items.summary: Singapore-based Megaspeed clarified that Alice Huang, linked by reports to Nvidia founder and former CEO Jensen Huang over US national security concerns, officially left the company on August 30, 2025 with no current role. The statement followed NYT reporting suggesting she is a Chinese intelligence asset tied to Huawei-linked stakes. Megaspeed declined to comment on her private matters.
items.title: Megaspeed Distances Alice Huang After Jensen Huang Affair Reports

items.summary: Jensen Huang reportedly told Jay Puri, 'I hope you die,' an incident described as unusually tense. A petition urging NVIDIA to reinstate him has drawn 133,326 signatures—mostly shareholders—with backing from Elon Musk, Amjad Masad and Tim Sweeney; the campaign is independent of NVIDIA.
items.title: 'I Hope You Die': Inside Jensen Huang's Ouster and the Stand-With-Jensen Campaign

items.summary: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Wallet in partnership with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, letting users add a card once while each purchase requires biometric verification. Initially available to Pro-tier subscribers via the Dots agent tool, it lets agents buy on any e-commerce site without brand plug-ins. The move follows competitors like Meta's Muse and xAI's Grok Bot, amid growing friction as brands block AI agents.
items.title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Wallet for AI-Driven Purchases

items.summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Sunday that India has secured an assurance of preferential market access in the United States, with Indian goods facing lower import duties than products from competing countries under a proposed bilateral trade agreement (BTA). The arrangement traces to broad framework agreements announced earlier this year by President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi. A senior government official noted both sides aim to conclude the first tranche by the end of the current financial year, though negotiations have been affected by changes in Washington's tariff regime after the Supreme Court struck down Trump's reciprocal tariffs.
items.title: India's Preferential US Market Access Under Proposed Trade Deal

items.summary: The Punjab Congress has formed a four-member committee to oversee the induction of leaders from other parties ahead of Assembly elections expected early next year. Constituted by state president Pargat Singh on Sunday, the panel includes Vijay Inder Singla, Aruna Chaudhary and Hardev Singh Laddi. It will consult local leadership before admitting new entrants as Congress strengthens its base for 2027.
items.title: Punjab Congress sets up panel to vet leaders joining from other parties ahead of 2027 polls

items.summary: Vinod Arya, father of convicted Pulkit Arya, demanded action against those who allegedly harassed victim Ankita Bhandari—her parents included. He stated the chats contained about 4,800 pages and that to his knowledge no VIP was involved; he denied any connection to elections or narrative steering. Throughout the chats, Ankita never mentioned Pulkit. The report is by Priyanka Jaiswal of The Times of India.
items.title: Convict's father demands action in Ankita Bhandari murder case

items.summary: A 26-year-old Bengaluru couple shared their monthly finances on Instagram, revealing total outgoings of ₹1,32,250 including a ₹60,000 SIP investment and ₹73,000 in other expenses. Their detailed breakdown—covering rent, utilities, commuting, groceries, gym memberships, and shopping—prompted online discussion about the high cost of living in India's technology hub.
items.title: Bengaluru Couple's ₹1.32 Lakh Monthly Budget Sparks Online Debate

items.summary: The Union Health Ministry released the National Health Accounts Estimates for India 2023-24, showing total health expenditure more than tripled from Rs 1.30 lakh crore in 2013-14 to Rs 4.14 lakh crore in 2023-24. Households' out-of-pocket share fell by 21.5 percentage points, from 64.2% to 42.7%, signaling stronger financial protection as government and insurance spending grew.
items.title: India's Health Spending Triples as Household Burden Falls

items.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of maligning India and PM Narendra Modi before an international audience, urging him to stop travelling abroad and visit villages instead. Shah said the party could remain out of power for another 30 years if it continued its course, alleging scams worth Rs 12 lakh crore during the Congress-led government's two terms from 2004 to 2014.
items.title: Amit Shah Accuses Rahul Gandhi of Defaming India on International Stage

items.summary: The ICC Board approved in Bali a schedule for major men's cricket events through 2035 and qualification formats for three global tournaments. The calendar spans four Men's T20 World Cups, two ODI World Cups, three World Test Championship finals and two Champions Trophies. India hosts the October 2029 Champions Trophy; India and Bangladesh co-host the November 2031 Cricket World Cup; England stages both WTC finals in June 2029 and 2031.
items.title: ICC finalises calendar till 2035: India to host 2029 Champions Trophy, co-host 2031 WC

items.summary: Mohan Kumar Maharana, a 47-year-old primary school teacher in Kandhamal district's Duba area, survived nearly two weeks stranded in a forest ravine after Cyclone Arnab triggered a landslide on October 29 that buried him near Dangesi village. Trapped and cut off by flooding and no mobile connectivity, he subsisted on muddy rainwater and edible forest food until a young goat herder heard his cries and alerted police and villagers. Rescuers trekked seven to eight kilometres through dense terrain before carrying him out on a makeshift stretcher; doctors found him extremely weak from starvation with cuts and injuries.
items.title: Odisha Teacher Survives 15-Day Ravine Ordeal After Cyclone Landslide

items.summary: This review celebrates M John Harrison's 2026 Booker Prize-winning novel The End of Everything as a marvel of weird fiction suited to our uncertain era. Set amid an alien invasion by the iGhetti, who confine themselves to London's Square Mile, it follows beachcomber Phillip Tennent and his aunt Marnie on a strange road trip through southeast England after discovering one of their adaptive artefacts. Harrison's violently fragmented yet structurally sound style resists conventional plot, drawing instead on an eclectic lineage spanning horror, fantasy and literary fiction rather than traditional science fiction.
items.title: Booker Prize winner ‘The End of Everything’ is a wonder of weird fiction for incomprehensible times

items.summary: The 49th ASEAN Summit opened in Manila on November 15, hosted by the Philippines under the theme 'Navigating Our Future, Together.' Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit from November 16 to 17 for the 23rd ASEAN-India and 21st East Asia Summits. Discussions focus on maritime cooperation—designated the 2026 ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation—and countering China in the South China Sea, where India insists any code of conduct comply with UNCLOS. Trade remains contentious: bilateral merchandise trade reached about USD 114 billion in 2025, though India's deficit grew from USD 7.5 billion in 2011 to USD 44 billion in 2023. Defence ties and regional crises also feature prominently.
items.title: ASEAN Summit in Manila and India's Strategic Interests

items.summary: Public disclosures under the Foreign Agents Registration Act reveal India's active media and diplomatic engagement with senior Trump administration officials. SHW Partners LLC, headed by Jason Miller, managed a $150,000 monthly contract for the Republic of India from April 2025 to June 2026, while Mercury Public Affairs coordinated only for the US Embassy of India. Filings show over two dozen exchanges focused on media coverage, including 44 calls discussing US-India relations and pitches for interviews with Ambassador Vinay Kwatra following Operation Sindoor.
items.title: India's US Lobbying Strategy Revealed in FARA Filings

items.summary: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner said his side let several chances slip across a closely-fought white-ball series against India, which they lost 1-3. Although New Zealand could have chased down targets like 210 and defended around 130 runs, the final ODI ended with India winning by 22 runs in five matches.
items.title: New Zealand Captain Santner Reflects on Lost Opportunities in Close India Series

items.summary: In Kolkata's Bikramgarh area, Sanjeev Bhattacharya allegedly killed his ex-girlfriend's two dogs after their breakup. He video-called her showing one dog hanged from a noose and crushed the puppy's head with a brick. The woman shared footage and alerted neighbors; both animals were found dead in the apartment. Jadavpur police arrested him, though reports suggest he may be mentally unstable.
items.title: Kolkata Man Kills Ex-Girlfriend's Two Dogs After Breakup; Arrested

items.summary: During the fifth ODI between India and New Zealand at Mount Maunganui on Sunday, a fan sitting in the grass banks offered their baby to Indian pacer Yash Thakur while he signed autographs near the boundary. Thakur declined the offer and continued signing memorabilia for spectators. The viral video gained social media attention as it marked his 50-over debut; Axar Patel presented him with his maiden ODI cap before he finished 1/38 in ten overs, taking Dean Foxcroft's wicket, as India won the series 3-1 by 22 runs.
items.title: Fan Offers Baby To Yash Thakur During IND vs NZ Autograph Session

items.summary: India's Parliament is expected to hold its Winter Session in the first week of December, with the Modi government prioritizing a constitutional amendment for 33% women's reservation in Parliament and state assemblies ahead of 2029 elections. The bill faces a two-thirds majority hurdle requiring at least 361 votes amid opposition resistance over electoral roll revisions (SIR) and demands to remove Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
items.title: Parliament Winter Session likely in December: Women's Reservation Bill, SIR row in focus

items.summary: The Economic Times reports three upcoming initial public offerings in India, set to raise over Rs 10,000 crore. Crystal Crop Protection's Rs 455 crore issue opens on November 18 and closes the next day; it combines a fresh share issuance of Rs 354.77 crore with an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs 100.71 crore by existing shareholders, backed by IIFL Capital Services as lead manager. Mahanadi Coalfields launches its entirely secondary OFS on November 19 to raise from parent Coal India; the company is India's largest coal producer and operates 17 mines in Odisha. Watrana Rentals follows with a Rs 120.10 crore SME IPO, priced at Rs 232-245 per share.
items.title: Three Indian IPOs Scheduled for Early November

items.summary: For Chhath Puja 2026's dawn offering (Usha Arghya) on Monday, November 16, Delhi Metro will begin services at 4:30 AM—an hour and a half earlier than the usual 6:00 AM start—running trains every 15 minutes across all lines until regular revenue services resume. BJP leader Pankaj Kumar Singh called it a 'major gift' for Purvanchal devotees, with DMRC confirming the schedule.
items.title: Delhi Metro Early Services for Chhath Puja Usha Arghya on November 16, 2026
